headline: Generative design balancing competing in silico objectives across molecules and fragments
label: Multi Objective Generative Drug Design
summary: Recent work pairs generative models with docking, RL, and QUBO optimization to balance competing in silico design objectives.
synthesis: The common thread is coupling generative or search procedures with explicit scoring, optimization, or constraint objectives in silico. ALCHIMIA combines RL-guided policy learning over 33 medicinal chemistry transformations with a genetic algorithm and docking to design molecules for CB2R. VeGA-RX and VeGA-SCX use SMARTS and scaffold guidance to control SMILES-based generative transformers. Q-SFD recasts simultaneous fragment docking as a QUBO problem with an inter-fragment distance term, roughly doubling top-1 recovery of linkable pose pairs, while LinkLlama fine-tunes Llama 3 on ChEMBL to generate linkers from text prompts. The bi-level diversity optimisation combines MaxMin and MaxSum objectives for representative protein panel selection. The LLM creativity study evaluates molecule generation across physicochemical, ADMET, and bioactivity tasks. What is new here is explicit handling of competing objectives across heterogeneous criteria; the summaries do not establish whether these trade-offs translate into experimental outcomes.
